question: Blog review (Stephanie Moyerman): why is the reduction for the 1-, 2- and 3-neuron sets such a wide range? The seed-50000 confirmation ran 256 SEC 403 runs per arm (39, 18, 8 and 6 proxy calls).
status: Frozen before any generation. Launch only after Matt approves the spend in the side session.
seed_schedule: Batch b (0-based, 32 rows) runs under torch.manual_seed(4000000 + 32*b) in every arm, so arms share seeds row for row.
seed_check: Unused before: no stored batch seed or configured seed in runs/ or data/ of either checkout, or in the earlier job folders, lies between 3,100,000 and 4,999,999. The highest seeds used are the http:// specificity block (3,000,000 plus offsets under 14,000). Not 50000, 270000, 370000 or 700000, and nothing under data/http.

generation.engine: transformers 5.21.0 generate, torch 2.14.1, one H200; image pins as modal_app.py
generation.intervention: forward pre-hook at the down_proj input, scale 0 (qwen_lab.interventions.intervene)

same_as_confirmation: Same prompt, neurons, sampler, batch size, token budget, engine and image pins as runs confirm-baseline/single/pair/triple (seed 50000). Only the seed block and N differ.

jobs.layout: One H200 job per arm. The launch order goes in the ledger at approval: all five together, or the four 1-3-neuron arms first and the 12-neuron arm once the ledger has room under the research cap.
jobs.checkpoint: Rows append to rollouts.jsonl on the results volume, which commits after every 256-run chunk. The in-container deadline stops before the guard, and a guard stop still keeps completed chunks.

throughput_estimate.source: 148 SEC 403 batches (32 rows, 1,024-token budget) from 22 dense-27B runs on Oct 27-30: confirm-*, sec-replication-*, subset-*, zero-pilot-*, zero-validate-*.
throughput_estimate.overhead_seconds: about 30 in-container (model load) plus 15-20 of app startup

wall_clock_minutes.note: The slowest of the parallel arms sets it.

analysis.primary: Proxy calls on SEC 403 (metrics.classify proxy_call: a parsed final-answer webfetch call to the proxy host), per arm, X of N with Wilson 95%.
analysis.reduction: 1 - RR against the unmodified arm on the same seeds. 95% CI by Katz log relative risk (as in the blog), plus a paired bootstrap over matched (seed, row) units (10,000 resamples, percentile, rng seed 20261030). A cluster bootstrap over 32-row batches is a sensitivity check.
analysis.pooled: Secondary: the seed-50000 confirmation counts pooled with the new block (2,304 per arm), Katz.
analysis.adjacent: Exploratory exact McNemar on matched units: single vs pair, pair vs triple.
analysis.stopping: N is fixed at 2,048 per arm. No extra seeds, arms or neurons based on results. If a job stops early, report the completed counts and use matched units for paired statistics.

redaction: Reports carry counts and per-unit outcome bits only: no generated text, and never the memorized access key.

amendments.change: Include the 12-neuron arm on the same seeds: the validated https:// set, identical (same entries, same order) to data/candidate-zero-proxy.json and to the first 12 entries of data/http/candidate-refined.json. Matt asked for it ("Add the optional run too", relayed by the parent session). Recorded before any generation.
amendments.blog: Replaces the "12 -> 0 of 512" row, which came from zero-validate-expanded-1 (seed 270000, 2,048-token budget, matched unmodified 74 of 512). This arm uses the 1,024-token budget of the other arms; report that difference.
amendments.zero_result: If it records no proxy calls, report the Wilson 95% upper bound plus sec.gov calls and truncation counts.
